chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtār from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) who said:
ʿĪbād al-Baṣrī asked him about a Mutamattiʿ (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattuʿ) who did not have a sacrificial animal with him. He said: "He should fast for three days before the Day of Tarwiyah."
He said: If the fasting of these days missed him, he said: "He should not fast the Day of Tarwiyah nor the Day of ʿArafah, but he should fast three consecutive days after the Days of Tashrīq."

This does not contradict what we mentioned, because he only negated the fasting of the Day of Tarwiyah in isolation, without negating that if he fasted it along with the Day of ʿArafah, as indicated by what we presented earlier. And whenever a person fasts before the Day of Tarwiyah and after the Days of Tashrīq, he only fasts consecutive days, as narrated.

key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, keeping the Ihram intact between them.
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: Sacrificial animal offered by the pilgrim.
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, the day pilgrims proceed to Mina.
key_terms.يَوْمُ عَرَفَةَ: The 9th of Dhul-Hijjah, the day of standing at Arafat.

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a Mutamattiʿ pilgrim who did not sacrifice an animal and missed the pre-Tarwiyah fasting days?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiʿ (AS) regarding the *dam* (expiation) for a Mutamattiʿ pilgrer lacking a sacrificial animal, prescribing three days of fasting if the pre-Tarwiyah fast is missed. The narration specifically clarifies that the exclusion of the Day of Tarwiyah applies when fasting in isolation, thereby harmonizing with other reports that permit fasting the Day of ʿArafah alongside it. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextual application of fasting prohibitions during the sacred days of Hajj.
